title: TinyEventEmitter & PromisePool
scenario: Build a typed event bus and a bounded asynchronous task coordinator for backend notification delivery.

milestones.title: Event Map & Listener Contracts
milestones.goal: Define generic event payloads and listener signatures so each event key remains associated with its payload type.

examples.input: emitter = new TinyEventEmitter(); typeof emitter.on('queued', listener)
examples.explanation: Subscribing to an event returns a release callback.
examples.call: (() => { const emitter = new TinyEventEmitter(); const release = emitter.on('queued', () => {}); return typeof release; })()

examples.explanation: Emitting a typed event delivers its matching payload to subscribed listeners.
examples.call: (() => { const log = []; const emitter = new TinyEventEmitter(); emitter.on('delivered', (p) => log.push(p.channel)); emitter.emit('delivered', { channel: 'email' }); return log; })()

milestones.title: on, off & emit
milestones.goal: Implement instance-owned event subscriptions, safe removal, registration-order delivery, and snapshot behavior for listeners added during delivery.

examples.input: Register two 'alert' listeners and emit { code: 'CPU_HIGH' }
examples.explanation: Listeners run in the order they were registered.
examples.call: (() => { const out = []; const e = new TinyEventEmitter(); e.on('alert', (p) => out.push('first:' + p.code)); e.on('alert', (p) => out.push('second:' + p.code)); e.emit('alert', { code: 'CPU_HIGH' }); return out; })()

examples.input: Subscribe to 'tick', emit 1, call release(), then emit 2
examples.explanation: Calling the release function stops subsequent deliveries to that listener.
examples.call: (() => { const seen = []; const e = new TinyEventEmitter(); const stop = e.on('tick', (n) => seen.push(n)); e.emit('tick', 1); stop(); e.emit('tick', 2); return seen; })()

examples.input: Register two 'sync' listeners, remove the first via off(), then emit {}
examples.call: (() => { const seen = []; const e = new TinyEventEmitter(); const dropped = () => seen.push('dropped'); e.on('sync', dropped); e.on('sync', () => seen.push('kept')); e.off('sync', dropped); e.emit('sync', {}); return seen; })()

milestones.title: Bounded PromisePool
milestones.goal: Execute task functions up to a validated concurrency limit, preserve input order, and capture each task outcome without stopping later tasks after one failure.

examples.explanation: Outcomes are returned in the original task order.
A failing task produces a rejected outcome without blocking remaining tasks.
examples.call: new PromisePool(2).run([() => 'ok', () => { throw new Error('timeout'); }, () => 'done']).then((res) => ({ statuses: res.map((r) => r.status), thirdValue: res[2].status === 'fulfilled' ? res[2].value : null }))

milestones.title: AbortSignal Cancellation & Cleanup
milestones.goal: Observe an optional AbortSignal, prevent queued tasks from starting after cancellation, preserve started outcomes, and release signal listeners when the pool settles.

examples.explanation: When the signal is not aborted, all tasks run to completion.
Once aborted, queued tasks do not start and resolve as rejected outcomes.
examples.call: (() => { const ac = new AbortController(); return new PromisePool(1).run([() => { ac.abort('stop'); return 'done'; }, () => 'skipped'], ac.signal).then((res) => res.map((r) => r.status)); })()
